title: Road of approach modelled from the sibling formations of the corps (history layer v6)
desc: No report of the Official Records read for the position ledgers (OR vol. 27) prints a road of approach for 56 leaf units (Longstreet's corps except Kershaw, Semmes, Wofford and Pickett's brigades; the Fifth Corps except the 20th Maine and Day's division) or for any formation above them. Each is drawn by the road that every documented sibling formation of its corps names (Chambersburg Pike for the First Corps, from Kershaw's report; Hanover Road for the Fifth Corps, from the 20th Maine row and Day's division report). The sibling formations may not have been on the road the unit used.
why: The record read so far does not state the unit's road; the primary sources are unread in part (EG-0005) and the Official Records give only some brigades' routes. Literal documentation of the road of these 56 units is not available from the repository.
searched: The four OR27 position ledgers (history/positions/positions_{A,B,C,D}.jsonl, 3,503 claims), every claim that names a road on the lines of command (APPROACH-AUDIT.md, data/sibling-review.json), the road-name concordance (library/ROAD-CONCORDANCE.md). Not yet searched: the regimental and brigade reports not in the ledgers, Busey and Martin, state regimental histories.
subst: Sibling-road rule (DEC-015): the units take the road documented for the other formations of their corps only if every documented sibling names the same road and no report on the unit's line of command names another road, a road the repository cannot place or a road outside the loaded ground (tools/sibling-rule.mjs, data/sibling-approach.json).
recon: A MODELLED road of approach (plausible-procedural). The unit's gate (never moved), its single-label Bachelder day position and its march from the edge of the ground are as for any other drawn unit; only the road, the minute at the edge and the place in the column are modelled.
marking: Card pill 'Modelled approach'; card text 'MODELLED APPROACH' with the siblings listed (report, page, printed words); provenance row 'Approach road (modelled)'; link to this entry; about panel paragraph.
impact: 56 leaf units (about 17,300 figures) in the First and Fifth Corps.
owner_q: Accept the sibling-road rule (DEC-015), reverse it (delete data/sibling-approach.json and the units return to open gaps) or require two or more documented siblings.
rec: Keep it as marked until the reports of the brigades are read; do not read it as history.

title: Faces, hair, facial hair, skin tone and body shape of every enlisted man (figure models)
desc: No record gives any enlisted man's face, hair, beard, complexion, stature or build (see EG-0001). The figure models generate every man from his manifest seed: 24 head shapes, 8 hair styles, 7 facial-hair types, 12 skin tones, 5 eye colours, 12 body shapes, stature 0.95-1.06 of 1.73 m. The mixes (facial hair 30/22/6/18/6/6/12 percent, hair colours, skin-tone weights, grey share 12 percent, coat-off share on 1-3 July) are tuning weights.
why: Literal 100% is impossible: individual appearance of the 165,000 men was not recorded. No anthropometric table, photograph survey or muster-roll physical description set was read for this task.
searched: kit/kit_specs.json (wear_states, no appearance data), PDF Part B.6 (dress only), render/PLAN.md G8 (variation targets). Not searched: enlistment descriptive rolls (height, complexion, hair, eyes are printed on Union enlistment papers: a possible source for sampled distributions), Gould 1869 anthropometry, CDV surveys.

title: Star count and arrangement of the US national colour
desc: The national colour is drawn with 34 stars on 13 stripes. No repository text states a star count for the flags at Gettysburg. The count rests on statutory reasoning recalled from memory (a star is added on the 4 July following an admission; West Virginia was admitted 20 June 1863, so 34 stars were in law on 1-3 July 1863): the lookup was NOT performed in this task. The arrangement (rows 6-5-6-5-6-6) is a plausible choice; period flags varied.
why: The record read so far does not describe any regiment's national colour; individual flags carried other star counts and arrangements.
searched: The repository (kit, PDF B.6, history layer): no star count. Not searched: the Flag Act of 1818 text, regimental colour catalogues (state flag collections), photographs of colours.
subst: A 34-star national colour; tier inferred (statutory reasoning) with the lookup recorded as not done.
recon: Stars and stripes with 34 stars in a plausible arrangement.
marking: Tier overlay on the flag; TIERS.json F-STAR-COUNT / F-STAR-ARRANGEMENT; FIGURES3D-NOTES.md.
impact: Every Union national colour drawn (the manifest gives a flag to a small share of men per unit).
